newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Springsteen shares music award with choirmaster.
newsitem.headline: Springsteen shares music award with choirmaster.

text.p: American rock star Bruce Springsteen shared centre stage with a Swedish choir master on Monday when he collected the 1997 Polar Music Prize, dubbed the Nobel prize for musicians.
Springsteen, known as "The Boss" to millions of fans around the world, was jointly awarded the the one million crown ($125,000) prize with choral conductor Eric Ericson.
The prize was established by Stikkan Anderson, former manager of pop group Abba, and is awarded to people, groups or institutions which have acted decisively in the world of music.
It is generally shared between a pop singer and a classical musician. Previous winners include Paul McCartney, Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Quincy Jones and Dizzy Gillespie.

Ericsson and Sprinsteen received the award from Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf at a ceremony in central Stockholm. Springsteen, 47, swapped his trademark jeans and open-necked shirt for a tuxedo for the occasion.
Ericson, 78, created Sweden's first professional choral group in 1946.
